core_obligations: Use the fibre product structure to write down the commutative diagram of rings and to identify the kernels of the horizontal maps on the module level (proof lines 553-566).
Treat the case of a prime of B whose image lies in A: construct a prime of B' lying over it with the required properties and verify primeness (proof lines 567-590).
Treat the case of a prime of A' whose image lies in A: construct the corresponding prime of B' and verify that it is prime and that it maps to the prescribed primes (proof lines 591-604).
Conclude that the points of Spec(B') are exactly the compatible pairs of points of Spec(B) and Spec(A'), which is the statement.
proof_roadmap: Write down the fibre product diagrams of rings and the corresponding kernels of the horizontal maps (proof lines 553-566).
For a prime of B whose contraction to A is contained in the given prime of A', build the corresponding prime of B' by a pullback construction and check primeness (proof lines 567-590).
For a prime of A' with the analogous compatibility, build the corresponding prime of B' and check primeness (proof lines 591-604).
Conclude the description of the points of Spec(B').
difficulty_reason: The lemma describes the points of the spectrum of the fibre product B' = B x_A A' by the points of Spec(B) and Spec(A') that agree over Spec(A), and its proof is a 52-line argument with several ingredients. It first uses the fibre product structure to produce commutative diagrams and identifies the kernels of the horizontal maps, then splits the discussion into the case where the prime considered is the inverse image of a prime of B or of A', and in each case has to construct a prime of the fibre product with prescribed behaviour. The constructions are carried out in full and include the verification that the ideals produced are prime, which is where the flatness of A over B is not needed but the exactness of the fibre product diagrams is.
